Use case: historical-scene. Single 3:2 landscape mature historical oil and gouache illustration, intimate father-son moment in a spacious late-Ming colonnade, clear soft daylight, indigo, warm timber and a restrained vermilion accent. Fuzhou in 1645, just after Zheng Sen has received the name Zheng Chenggong. Zheng Zhilong reaches up to smooth his son's turned collar, his hand hesitating as the young man is about to go to waiting officials. A household attendant steps aside. Father: early forties, solid build, long oval Fujian Han face, straight brows, deep-set eyes, slightly broad nostrils, fine mustache with slight gray, simple Ming cap and sober formal robe. Son: twenty-one, slim, clean-shaven, straight eyebrows, more delicate long face, neat Ming robe and cap over tied hair. Their eye contact and collar gesture dominate; officials remain secondary figures at the far end. Do not show a grand coronation, invented imperial regalia or exact rank badges. No Qing queues, modern objects, readable text, title, watermark or collage.
Reference roles: image 1 is only a youthful face and naturalistic historical-style reference for Zheng Zhilong, the man holding the rope. Age that same face into a believable man in his early forties. Image 2 shows this father and his son at age six in an earlier chapter; use only the child's familial facial traits to imagine the son as a full-height twenty-one-year-old ADULT here. There are NO CHILDREN in this new picture. Father and son must be visibly different generations, with father about forty-one and son twenty-one. Do not copy any peripheral reference people, cargo, ship, rope, waterfront, stone quay, clothing pose or background. Create the entirely new indoor-outdoor government colonnade specified above, not a harbor. Naturalistic tactile realism matching references, restrained painterly finish. One separate full-frame artwork, not a collage or a revision of the reference.

Use case: historical-scene. Single 3:2 landscape mature historical narrative illustration in restrained oil and gouache, clear side-window daylight, warm timber, deep indigo and pale paper. Fujian Zheng household, spring 1645. Zheng Hongkui firmly holds open a ship register so an attendant cannot replace it, while his elder brother Zheng Zhilong pauses with a brush above the page; Chen Qian sits nearby witnessing their difficult allocation of ships and experienced crew. Hongkui's travel-ready subordinates wait by the doorway. Zheng Zhilong in his early forties has a long oval face, straight eyebrows, deep-set eyes, slightly broad nostrils, fine mustache with a little gray, plain dark Ming cap and dignified indigo robe. Hongkui is a distinct adult with family resemblance, somewhat narrower face, practical belted robe and determined posture. Use simple late-Ming timber furniture, no imperial throne or exact rank emblems. The open ledger shows blurred brush marks only. No Qing queues, modern objects, text, caption, watermark or collage; do not portray Hongkui as a passive subordinate.
Reference role: use image 1 only for the long-oval face of young Zheng Zhilong gripping the rope and the naturalistic tactile historical art style. Render Zheng Zhilong in his early forties with maturity and a slightly graying fine mustache. Do not reuse the reference's other people as Hongkui, Chen Qian or attendants: design them as distinct named roles. Hongkui is his adult younger brother, not his son. Do not reproduce the harbor, ship, cargo, clothing pose, ropes or stone quay; this entire scene is inside a Fujian household meeting room. The ledger pressed down by Hongkui, Zhilong's hovering brush, and Chen Qian observing are the central action. One independent complete frame.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit only the distant background visible between the left-hand red columns in this historical illustration. Replace the entire harbor, water, ships, far shore and mountains with a believable enclosed internal courtyard of a modest late-Ming Fuzhou administrative compound in 1645: pale plaster perimeter wall, gray roof tiles, a covered connecting corridor, stone paving and one small tree. No water, boats, sails, quay, coastal horizon or mountain panorama anywhere. Preserve exactly the two foreground adult father-and-son faces, ages, physique, hats, clothing, father smoothing son's collar, attendant stepping aside, distant waiting officials, red columns, daylight, camera framing, composition and naturalistic painterly texture. Father remains early forties, son twenty-one, no children. This is the same intimate departure moment and the building is an artistic reconstruction, not an exact palace plan. No text, watermark, collage or modern objects. Single 3:2 landscape image.

Use case: historical-scene. Single 3:2 landscape mature oil and gouache historical illustration, warm domestic humor in honest daylight, pale plaster, timber brown, muted indigo and soft neutral cloth. Anping household, autumn 1645. Tagawa quietly repeats a familiar Japanese phrase to her grown son Zheng Chenggong, who listens closely and tries again, smiling at his own difficulty; Zheng Zhilong beside them has also tried and looks affectionately embarrassed. A small packet of silver and an unreadable message intended for the younger son in Japan rest on a simple table. Tagawa is a Japanese woman in her early forties, oval face, straight eyebrows, dark hair modestly tied up, plain muted kosode and narrow sash, no elaborate geisha makeup or oversized obi. Chenggong is a slim clean-shaven twenty-one-year-old with straight brows and delicate long face, Ming robe and tied hair; Zheng Zhilong is early forties, long oval face, fine mustache with slight gray, indigo robe and Ming cap. Natural unstaged gestures, no posed group portrait. No Qing queues, readable text, title, watermark or collage.
Reference roles: image 1 supplies ONLY the two distinct adult male identities: the mustached older man at left is the father, the clean-shaven young adult at right is the son. Keep these identities and ages but completely change their pose, actions and setting to the seated household conversation described here. Image 2 supplies ONLY the woman's facial identity; she was pregnant in that earlier chapter, but now she is about forty-one, NOT PREGNANT, with natural mature facial lines and the same basic oval face. The young man in image 2 is NOT an additional cast member: do not copy him. There are exactly three main adults and NO CHILDREN or baby in this image; the younger son is still in Japan and absent. The mother speaks, the adult son smiles while carefully repeating her words, and father listens with affectionate embarrassment. All are in a completely enclosed plaster-and-timber domestic room with a simple table, diffuse window light, no visible harbor, ships, mountains, red government colonnade or former stage setting. One independent complete scene; only likeness/style comes from references, not their locations or actions.

Use case: historical-scene. Single 3:2 landscape mature historical oil and gouache illustration, strong readable action in plain river daylight, gray water, brown wood and indigo. Nanjing river landing, 1644. Young Zheng Sen stands on the unstable boarding plank of a requisitioned passenger boat, grasping the tip of an official runner's wooden staff to make space for a mother carrying her child. Her bundle has split and ordinary clothes lie near their feet. Zheng Sen, about twenty, slim long youthful face, straight eyebrows and delicate features resembling Zheng Zhilong, clean-shaven, wears a modest Ming scholar's robe and cloth cap over tied hair. His strained hand and braced body show he has been knocked against the boat rail; the runner is frustrated rather than monstrous. Frame at plank height so the woman's unstable footing and the river gap remain legible. Other passengers wait, no monumental invented city skyline. No Zheng Zhilong present. No Qing queues, modern clothing, gore, readable notices, title, watermark or collage. This specific intervention is the novel's reconstruction.
Reference role: image 1 supplies ONLY the identity of the younger clean-shaven adult son on the RIGHT, not the older father on the left. Render that same son at about twenty years of age; he is the only Zheng-family member in the new scene. DO NOT include his father or mother from prior family images. The woman carrying a child is a separate anonymous passenger, in plain modest clothing; design her and the official runner as distinct people, not copies of reference faces. Change all poses and setting: this is a muddy river landing at Nanjing with a small ordinary passenger boat, NOT the reference's government corridor or earlier Hirado/Fujian seaport. Show a narrow timber gangplank bridging the boat-bank gap; the son's feet are grounded on that plank, one hand firmly arrests the runner's staff tip, and the mother has space to steady herself with her child. Do not stage a sword fight, shove the child into danger, or depict graphic injury. Keep tactile naturalistic historical realism and one independent full-frame narrative moment.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Keep this single 3:2 historical illustration exactly the same except the uniform and staff of the man at the far RIGHT. He is a low-ranking official runner doing boat requisition work in Nanjing, 1644, not a court minister: replace his tall winged official hat and square embroidered chest badge with a plain modest dark cloth cap and practical unadorned dark short work robe with a simple cloth belt. Remove all rank insignia, chest emblems and lavish gold decoration from his clothing. Change the staff into a plain, slightly worn brown hardwood pole with NO metal or gold bands or ornamental fittings. Preserve the runner's face and restrained frustrated expression, his posture and hands, and the exact gripping interaction with the young man. Preserve the entire young Zheng Sen face and pose, grounded feet on the narrow plank, the mother carrying her child, spilled clothes, waiting passengers, boat, river daylight, background, natural materials, color and camera framing. Do not add/remove any characters or objects other than replacing the specified costume/staff details. No readable text, watermark, collage, graphic injury, Qing queue or modern objects.
